text.title: Program Dependency Aging Chart Recipe — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete Monday chart for a five-team checkout program: five open edges from a 48-day API contract with a cut-scope decision to a 4-day no-deadline environment edge, a re-ticketed security review that keeps its original age, a young edge with negative slack at the top of the table, twelve resolved edges giving an SLE of 33 days, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the same week as it is usually shown, with what the validator prints and what the program PM misses.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Program `checkout-replatform`, five teams (payments, platform, web, data, security), weekly checkpoint on Mondays, program PM program-pm:olena. Chart date 2026-09-07; the script ran at 07:30 that morning. Bands were adopted on 2026-05-04 at the recipe default. Security closed SEC-7 on 2026-09-01 and opened SEC-9 for the same review the next day.

example.title: checkout-replatform, chart date 2026-09-07
example.note: 2026-09-07 is a Monday and the extraction ran that morning, so the chart is this checkpoint's (r-weekly-refresh-by-script). PLAT-118 is 48 days old counted from the link's creation on 2026-07-21, although platform commented on it last Friday; it sits in the open top band, so it carries both an action and Olena's `cut-scope` decision (r-age-from-dependency-open-not-task, r-action-per-escalation-band). WEB-402 is only 18 days old but its milestone date passed three days ago: `slack_days` -3 puts it red and first in `action_table`, ahead of the older PLAT-118 (r-milestone-slack-column). SEC-9 was opened on 2026-09-02 but `superseded_from: SEC-7` gives it SEC-7's `opened_at` of 2026-08-12 and 26 days of age; SEC-7 is not in `resolved_log`, because a review closed and reopened within 14 days was never closed (r-no-aging-reset). After the red edge the table runs band descending, then blocked count: SEC-9 (15-28, 1) before DATA-77 (8-14, 1) before PLAT-131 (0-7, 3) (r-count-blocked-tasks-per-edge). PLAT-131 has no `needed_by`, so slack is null and it is plotted as no-deadline; it is in the first band and carries no action yet (r-typed-edges-from-graph). Twelve edges resolved since 2026-06-15 (the trailing 12 weeks) have ages 9 to 41; the 85th percentile by nearest rank is the 11th value, 33 days, drawn as the SLE line above the 28-day band boundary, which tells Olena that a 3-week turnaround is not what this program does (r-closed-edges-feed-sle). DATA-60 could be closed `not-needed` because it had a `needed_by`; WEB-381 never had one and was delivered.

section.title: The same week as it is usually shown

example.title: last-activity clock, re-cut bands, waiting-on actions
example.note: What the validator prints: PLAT-118's action reads "Waiting on platform", which the pattern rejects (r-action-per-escalation-band); `sle.status: line` with 2 resolved edges and no `p85_days` (r-closed-edges-feed-sle). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks fire: `extracted_at` is two weeks before the chart date, so this is last fortnight's chart touched up in a slide (r-weekly-refresh-by-script); PLAT-118 shows 3 days because the script counted from the last comment, while `chart_date` minus `opened_at` is 48 (r-age-from-dependency-open-not-task); WEB-402 has slack -3 and no action, and sits last in `action_table` instead of first (r-milestone-slack-column, r-action-per-escalation-band). What the program PM sees at the checkpoint: a green chart with nothing over 14 days. What she does not see: the top band was quietly moved from 28 to 45 days after a bad August (fm-03), SEC-7 was closed on 2026-09-01 and reopened as SEC-9 the next day with a fresh clock and no `superseded_from`, so a 26-day review reads as 5 (fm-04), and the milestone that WEB-402 was needed for slipped three days ago with the edge in the lowest band (fm-06).
